properties.name: jinja2cpp:used-for
properties.value: nonstd::expected behind jinja2::Result<T> in every Load/Render signature (include/jinja2cpp/template.h, template_env.h); make_unexpected in parsers and bindings

properties.name: jinja2cpp:why
properties.value: C++17 has no std::expected; the 2.0 API returns Result<T> (docs/api-2.0.md decision 4), and Clang 18 + libstdc++ at C++23 ships <expected> without std::expected

properties.name: jinja2cpp:lighten
properties.value: Keep until a C++23 floor. Header-only and small; could be vendored into include/ so consumers need nothing extra, at the cost of an ODR clash with a consumer's own expected-lite of another version

properties.name: jinja2cpp:conan-why
properties.value: ConanCenter has expected-lite 0.9.0 at most (checked 2026-10-24); conan-build stays one version behind until 0.10.0 is published there

properties.name: jinja2cpp:used-for
properties.value: Python str.format / format filter and %-formatting (src/python_format.cpp, serialize_filters.cpp, value_methods.cpp), number-to-string, wide-string formatting (fmt/xchar.h), error messages (error_info.cpp), the string builder's memory_buffer

properties.name: jinja2cpp:why
properties.value: Python's format-spec mini-language with runtime format strings, precision-as-argument and wchar_t output; std::format is C++20 and the floor is C++17

properties.name: jinja2cpp:lighten
properties.value: Keep. Could be built header-only (FMT_HEADER_ONLY) to remove the link-time dependency of static consumers, at a compile-time cost; replace with std::format only at a C++20 floor (wide output and runtime specs still need checking)

properties.name: jinja2cpp:selected-by
properties.value: boost_json in JINJA2CPP_TEST_BINDINGS (default nlohmann_json) with JINJA2CPP_BUILD_TESTS: internal mode fetches the release for the Boost.JSON binding test and never installs it; external, external-boost and conan-build find a system Boost >= 1.75 (Conan: header-only) only when a Boost piece is selected. Consumers: the components jinja2cpp::boost_json and jinja2cpp::boost_multiprecision find it when requested (docs/tasks/0311)

properties.name: jinja2cpp:used-for
properties.value: The opt-in components only: Boost.JSON for the boost_json binding and its test, and Multiprecision with Config (boost-multiprecision, boost-config, fetched on their own) for the bigint=boost backend and the boost_multiprecision adapter. The library links no Boost and the core package never names it (0230 D7a); only a Boost component's own files find Boost (0311)

properties.name: jinja2cpp:why
properties.value: The components jinja2cpp::boost_json and jinja2cpp::boost_multiprecision (bindings/boost_*) are public opt-in API, so CI keeps testing them (bindings.yml)

properties.name: jinja2cpp:lighten
properties.value: Done (docs/tasks/0230): span, small_vector, intrusive_ptr, unique_any, iterator_facade, the string algorithms, endian, filesystem and Boost.JSON metadata parsing have own replacements; scripts/sbom.py --check keeps <boost/ out of every other file

properties.name: jinja2cpp:conan-why
properties.value: ConanCenter has Boost 1.91.0 at most (checked 2026-10-24); conanfile.txt takes it header_only, and Boost is only an optional adapter dependency and test-only (0230)
